title: The Morning Digest: November 19, 2026
dek: Brent Jan27 settled $91.95, down $1.19 or 1.3 percent, and WTI Dec26 settled $83.26, down $2.75 or 3.2 percent on Wednesday (Reuters, Nov 18), and Asia held the level at Brent $92.00 and WTI $83.00 at 0455 GMT on Thursday (Reuters, Nov 19), with the Brent to WTI spread at $8.69. The official inventory report for the week ending Nov 13 printed crude up 3.380 million barrels against a survey consensus of 1.0 million. December Mainline apportionment is Light 24 percent and Heavy 17 percent at Kerrobert (Enbridge notice, announced Nov 18), up from November's 19 and 7 percent. January WCS settled -$23.45 (ICE TMW settle, Nov 18). The validated diesel crack is $80.34 on the latest print.

sources.vintage: Nov 19, 2026 (overnight tape at 0455 GMT: Brent Jan27 $92.00, up five cents; WTI Dec26 $83.00, down 26 cents; WTI Jan27 $82.09 ahead of the December contract expiry on Nov 20)

Nov 18, 2026 (Russian refining processing down about 45 percent point to point since late October on two industry sources, from above 700,000 tonnes a day to about 400,000, with 15 of 35 major refineries disrupted; average November processing above 500,000 tonnes a day, only 5 to 10 percent below September and October, so the 45 percent figure is not a monthly average; Ilsky and Afipsky refineries struck Nov 17 and overnight Nov 18, four injured per Russian officials, damage not independently verified)

Nov 13, 2026 (October global supply 105.4 million barrels a day, up 2.3 million on the month, above demand for the first time since the war began; Gulf exports still 26 percent below pre-war) (6d old)
